blindSummary:
This country combines some of the world's strongest legal protections for transgender people with a high level of real-world violence — the classic gap between law and practice. Courts allow name and gender-marker changes without surgery, the supreme court has criminalised transphobia (making it punishable like racism), courts fine businesses that discriminate, and official guidance affirms trans people's right to use bathrooms matching their identity.

For visitors, big-city queer life is vibrant and highly visible — the country's largest city hosts the world's largest Pride parade — and the law is unambiguously on a trans traveller's side. The practical risks are concentrated in nightlife and app-based meetings: a majority of physical violence against LGBTQIA+ people in the largest city happens at night, and robbery schemes luring gay men via dating apps have been fatal.

Exercise particular caution after dark, with nightlife and app meetings, and in outlying districts. Violence against local trans people (this country records the world's highest absolute toll of killings of trans people) is heavily concentrated in poor and marginalised communities, not tourist areas.
blindOutOfScope: The general crime problem (armed robbery, kidnappings, gang violence) leads foreign governments to advise a high degree of caution for every traveller.
blindSourceSummaries: Encyclopedia overview of LGBT rights in this country: covers the 2018 supreme-court rulings on gender identity (self-declaration of gender marker; name/gender change without surgery), non-binary recognition, healthcare, conversion-therapy ban, anti-LGBT violence, and social conditions. Same-sex marriage recognised since 2013.

International LGBT-rights organisation country overview (updated March 2026): marriage equality since 2013 (with congressional repeal efforts underway); a 2019 supreme-court ruling prohibits discrimination and hate crimes based on SOGI; trans people can change gender markers by self-determination. The country continues to have one of the highest rates of violence against sexual and gender minorities, particularly trans people; 3,000+ openly LGBTQ candidates ran in the 2024 municipal elections.

Local law-firm guide (April 2026) for expats: same-sex marriage, spousal-visa equality, adoption, and name/gender-marker changes are available; notes there is no comprehensive federal anti-discrimination statute, with protections built from court rulings.

Investigative journalism outlet (May 2024): inquiry into violence against LGBTQIA+ people in the nightlife of the country's largest city - 57% of physical-violence incidents against LGBTQIA+ people in that city occurred at night; victims report insecurity in bars and clubs.
